motifReview.reviewerStatement: I independently compared this asset and its source record against R1 (docs/exec-50304c60-4218-4f0b-b73f-27b218d4b941.png) and R2 (docs/exec-cb613d03-7a77-4266-bd6b-e0d83428f067.png) using every motif checklist row. I read both references at full size, made close-up crops of the highest-risk regions (R1 card back, R1 teal wisp art window, R2 deck-back stacks), read all four rendered crops plus cards-full.png, and inspected the authored SVG path geometry in src/presentation/cards/art/golden-sample-art.js line by line. I found no traced or closely copied silhouette, composition, ornament path, or motif; all similarity is confined to the deliberately shared sampled palette/material mood and generic TCG layout conventions, which I document explicitly below rather than certify silently.

rows.evidence: Compared subjects: the asset depicts a stone spring/fountain erupting a column of mana light, while R1/R2's mana motif is a floating teardrop wisp; the object identity differs.

Compared focal composition against a close-up crop of the R1 teal art: a full-height symmetric light spire rising from a pool between corner foliage masses (lines 113-137) versus R1's small droplet hovering over a flat flower-and-rock field; the silhouettes are unrelated.

Verified the wisp form specifically: R1's wisp is a round-bottomed teardrop with a curling pointed tip and white core; the asset contains no teardrop anywhere - its orbiting accents are plain circles and its spring stones are smooth quads/ellipses, not R1's faceted low-poly rocks.
Compared the fang-in-teal-oval divider emblem against the R1 teal card's multi-point compass rosette at the same slot; the position convention matches but no rosette point geometry is reused.
Compared frames: flat teal band with rounded corners versus R1's beveled teal metal frame with corner-cut art window, corner ornaments, and edge filigree; no ornament path carried over.
Card face; no card-back sigil, constellation, or rotational-cue content to compare.

Compared environment props: the corner foliage masses are two smooth quadratic blobs (lines 109-110) rather than low-poly canopy clusters, and the ground is flat bands with no copy of R1's scattered-flower-and-rock prop map.
Compared text and badges: English rules text versus pseudo-glyph strings, and the mana '0' sits in a plain cream circle versus R1's octagonal shield-shaped badge.
The teal family (#277A79/#8FD8CB), gold core (#F5D783), and parchment are deliberately sampled per the art direction; the retention is confined to color/material roles.

Both cards read as 'teal cast card with glowing cyan magic above grey stones' - a subject-family echo that follows from the sanctioned palette/mood guidance - but I traced every path (spire, pool, stones, droplets) and each is independently constructed geometry, not a redrawn reference form.
